title: The Black Cat band with Lonnie Simmons and Freddie Green
summary: His first decent New York job: a quintet with Simmons, Freddie Green, Frank Clarke and Bobby Moore at the Black Cat, where Goodman, Harry James and Basie jammed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So Frank got this job at the Black Cat.

Yeah. And he told Lonnie Simmons, the bandleader, about me, so Lonnie hires me. So there was Freddie Green, Lonnie Simmons, Frank Clarke, Bobby Moore, who was the little trumpet player who played, "Out the Window," with Basie, remember?
That little trumpet player. He was working with us. So like we had trumpet, tenor, piano, bass and guitar. That was our band. And what a band that was.
And Lonnie Simmons was a friend of Freddie's from --
That's right, from Charleston or somewhere.
Well, wait a minute. Let's see --
No. They're from South Carolina. I can't think of it.
But I know it very well.

So what happend is that the rhythm section was so fantastic until everybody used to come and jam at the Black Cat. Benny Goodman, Harry James, Basie, Lionel, because I had vibraphones. And everyone used to come there and --
And this was practically your first job in New York.

Yeah, it was my first job really. My first decent job, you know. So everyone used to come and jam, and I'd look around -- the boss's name was Frankel, and Frankel used to keep Benny Goodman used to keep us there till 9:00 o'clock in the morning. And Harry used to come right by
the sock cymbal with his trumpet and blow into the sock cymbal.

Can you imagine? And Basie used to come all the time with Benny, you know, and jam with us. And that's when he got the idea, the way the rhythm section was jumping, he just took Freddie right out. I imagine if Joe hadn't been with the band I would probably have joined the band, too, you know.
Because the rhythm section was so perfect and I used to see a little crew cut guy in the audience, bobbing his head and weaving, and it was John Hammond.
Every night. Just about every night. I think he was going to Columbia University at the time. And this little crew cut guy was jumping up and down.
